 PETRA urged to address flooding, river erosion and electricity supply issues
 November 19, 2026 
 0 
 82 
 Facebook Twitter Pinterest WhatsApp 
 KUALA LUMPUR: The Energy Transition and Water Transformation Ministry (PETRA) has been urged to address long-standing issues of flooding, riverbank erosion and electricity supply affecting residents in Sipitang and Beaufort.
 Sipitang MP Datuk Matbali Musah said the three critical issues required comprehensive and lasting solutions.
 He called on PETRA to consider allocating special funds for comprehensive flood mitigation projects and upgrading the existing drainage systems in both districts.
 He said overflowing waters from Sungai Mengalong, coupled with drainage systems that could no longer cope with the water flow, had caused frequent flooding in 17 villages under the Sindumin Scheme, with floodwaters taking more than a week to recede in some areas.
 He also called for urgent dredging, deepening and rehabilitation works at the estuaries of Sungai Sipitang and Sungai Mengalong.
 “This is important as sedimentation not only obstructs the flow of water into the sea but also makes it difficult for fishermen’s boats and enforcement agency vessels to navigate during low tide,” he said during the committee-level debate on PETRA’s budget in the Dewan Rakyat yesterday.
 Matbali said residents in the Lumadan state constituency were also grappling with floods, with nine incidents recorded throughout 2025 following the overflowing of Sungai Padas and Sungai Bukau.
 Among the affected areas were Kampung Luagan Sanginan, Suasa, Kebajang, Bangkalalak, Mentulud, Bukau and Lingkungan.
 Meanwhile, riverbank erosion has also become increasingly critical in several areas within the Lumadan constituency, including Kampung Lubak, the cemeteries in Kampung Lupak and Beringin, as well as Kampung Kaundo, Suasa and Luagan Sanginan.
 On electricity supply, Matbali urged the ministry to build new electrical substations in Kampung Lalangut, Suasa, Kukup, Bangkalalak and Weston to address the long-standing problem of low voltage affecting residents.
 “We are also urging the ministry to upgrade the existing bare electrical cables in Kampung Weston to insulated cables to ensure public safety, as well as replace 150 streetlights in the Lumadan Zone,” he said.
